faqs.question: Why do some calendars show Ganesh Chaturthi 2027 starting on 3 September?
faqs.answer: The Chaturthi tithi begins at 02:18 PM on 3 September 2027 and ends at 12:25 PM on 4 September. The festival day is the 4th, because that is the day the tithi is running at midday; the 3rd is only when the tithi opens.

faqs.question: How many days does Ganeshotsav run in 2027?
faqs.answer: Ten. Sthapana is Saturday 4 September 2027 and visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi is Tuesday 14 September 2027, one day shorter than the eleven-day stretch in 2026.

faqs.question: Why is the gap between Ganesh Chaturthi and visarjan not always ten days?
faqs.answer: The two ends are fixed by different tithis that drift independently of each other. Across 2026 to 2031 the gap runs eleven days in 2026, ten in 2027, 2028 and 2029, and nine in 2030 and 2031.

faqs.question: Why is the 2027 puja muhurat so much shorter than 2026's?
faqs.answer: The madhyahna window cannot outlast the Chaturthi tithi, and in 2027 that tithi expires at 12:25 PM, part-way through midday. Mumbai gets 1 hour 3 minutes on 4 September 2027 against 2 hours 27 minutes on 14 September 2026.

faqs.question: What time should I avoid looking at the moon on 4 September 2027?
faqs.answer: Drik Panchang marks 09:49 AM to 09:16 PM on 4 September 2027. It marks a second window of 02:18 PM to 08:34 PM on the evening of 3 September, because the tithi starts that afternoon.

faqs.question: Does Ganesh Chaturthi 2027 fall on a weekend?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4 September 2027 is a Saturday. Visarjan on 14 September is a Tuesday, so the immersion procession lands mid-week.

faqs.question: Can Ganesh Chaturthi ever fall in July or October?
faqs.answer: No. Across the fourteen years Drik Panchang lists from 2024 to 2037, the earliest is 23 August 2028 and the latest 20 September 2031. The adhika masa pulls the date back inside that band of roughly one month whenever the drift gets too large.

faqs.question: What exactly is a tithi?
faqs.answer: A tithi is one-thirtieth of a synodic month, defined as the time the angular distance between the Sun and the Moon takes to widen by 12 degrees. It averages about 23 hours 37 minutes, so it slides against the calendar day and can begin or end at any hour.

faqs.question: Does the Ganesh Chaturthi date repeat on a cycle?
faqs.answer: Roughly every nineteen years. Nineteen tropical years come to 6,939.6018 days and 235 synodic months to 6,939.6886 days, so the solar and lunar calendars almost re-align — the Metonic cycle — drifting only about two hours each time round.

faqs.question: How far ahead can these dates be trusted?
faqs.answer: NASA publishes lunar phases to the year 2100 and panchang software computes decades ahead, so the astronomy is not the limiting factor. The residual uncertainty is in how a given almanac applies its sunrise and midday rules, which is why two panchangs occasionally print a festival a day apart.

faqs.question: Is Ganesh Chaturthi 2027 the same date everywhere in India?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4 September 2027 on every Indian city page checked, from Chennai to New Delhi. What differs is the muhurat: Chennai's madhyahna window opens at 10:54 AM and Mumbai's at 11:23 AM, and both close at 12:25 PM.

faqs.question: How early should I send an invitation for 4 September 2027?
faqs.answer: Production is not the constraint — the median gap between a SubhSandesh page's first save and its last edit is 6.8 hours, sampled across 1,065 pages, platform-wide rather than Ganesh-specific. Send it two to three weeks out if you want people to book travel around a Saturday sthapana.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ganesh Chaturthi 2027: Saturday 4 September, and Why It Moved

Ganesh Chaturthi 2027 falls on **Saturday, 4 September 2027**, and visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi falls on **Tuesday, 14 September 2027**. That is ten days earlier than 2026, and the madhyahna puja window in Mumbai runs just 1 hour 3 minutes — 11:23 AM to 12:25 PM — against 2 hours 27 minutes this year.

The first-party numbers on this page are **platform-wide across all 15 SubhSandesh page types**, not Ganesh-specific: 49.6% of shared pages are opened on a phone (22,667 of 45,656 views) and 96.1% of started pages are actually published and shared (3,708 of 3,860), both measured 2026-09-08. Below are the dates to 2031 with visarjan attached, the arithmetic behind them, and a check you can run yourself.

## Ganesh Chaturthi 2027 date, muhurat and visarjan

[Drik Panchang's 2027 page for Mumbai](https://www.drikpanchang.com/festivals/ganesh-chaturthi/ganesh-chaturthi-date-time.html?geoname-id=1275339&year=2027) puts the Chaturthi tithi from 02:18 PM on 3 September to 12:25 PM on 4 September. The festival day is the 4th.

That 12:25 PM ending is what makes 2027 awkward. The madhyahna window cannot outlast the tithi, so every Indian city's puja muhurat closes at the same instant that day — and the further west you are, the less of it you get.

| City | Madhyahna Ganesha puja muhurat, 4 Sep 2027 | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Chennai | 10:54 AM – 12:25 PM | 1 h 31 m |
| Hyderabad | 11:01 AM – 12:25 PM | 1 h 25 m |
| New Delhi | 11:04 AM – 12:25 PM | 1 h 21 m |
| Bengaluru | 11:05 AM – 12:25 PM | 1 h 21 m |
| Mumbai | 11:23 AM – 12:25 PM | 1 h 03 m |

Two moon-sighting windows are marked for avoidance: 02:18 PM to 08:34 PM on 3 September, and 09:49 AM to 09:16 PM on 4 September.

## Why 2027 lands ten days earlier than 2026

Twelve lunar months do not add up to a solar year. Gislén and Eade's 2019 survey of lunisolar calendars in the *Journal of Astronomical History and Heritage* states it directly: a solar year is ["about 11 days longer than a lunar year with 12 synodic months"](https://web.archive.org/web/20240827060635/https://www.narit.or.th/files/JAHH/2019JAHHvol22/2019JAHH...22..407G.pdf), which comes to roughly 354 days.

So a festival pinned to a lunar tithi walks backwards through the Gregorian year. [NASA's century-long table of lunar phases](https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/phase/phases2001.html) puts the new moon that opens Bhadrapada at 03:27 UT on 11 September 2026 and the next one at 17:41 UT on 31 August 2027 — 354 days apart, almost exactly the figure above.

The festival itself shifted ten days, not eleven, and the missing day is the tithi rule doing its work. In 2026 the Chaturthi began at 07:06 AM on the 14th; in 2027 it begins at 02:18 PM on the 3rd and is still running at midday on the 4th, so the 4th claims it.

## The extra month that resets the drift

Left alone, eleven days a year would drag Ganesh Chaturthi out of the monsoon and into winter inside two decades. The Hindu calendar prevents that by inserting a thirteenth month.

Gislén and Eade give the mechanism: because a synodic month is shorter than a solar month, "there will sometimes be two lunar months starting in the same solar month", and the first of that pair becomes intercalary — the adhika masa, carrying the same name with *adhika* in front of it.

Averaged out, this lands on the Metonic pattern: seven intercalary months in nineteen years, 235 lunations in total. The same paper does the arithmetic — nineteen tropical years is 6,939.6018 days, 235 synodic months is 6,939.6886 days, a mismatch of about two hours per cycle.

You can watch the resets happen in the next five years. The date drops ten days into 2027 and twelve more into 2028, then jumps *forward* nineteen days into 2029, back ten into 2030, and forward nineteen again into 2031. NASA's table agrees: the gaps between governing new moons run 354, 355, 384, 353 and 384 days, and each 384-day gap is a year with an extra month in it.

## Ganesh Chaturthi for the next five years

Every date below was read off Drik Panchang's per-year page for Mumbai and cross-checked against NASA's new-moon instants.

| Year | Ganesh Chaturthi | Visarjan | Madhyahna muhurat, Mumbai | Days of Ganeshotsav |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 | Mon 14 Sep | Fri 25 Sep | 11:20 AM – 01:48 PM | 11 |
| 2027 | Sat 4 Sep | Tue 14 Sep | 11:23 AM – 12:25 PM | 10 |
| 2028 | Wed 23 Aug | Sat 2 Sep | 11:25 AM – 01:57 PM | 10 |
| 2029 | Tue 11 Sep | Fri 21 Sep | 11:21 AM – 01:49 PM | 10 |
| 2030 | Sun 1 Sep | Tue 10 Sep | 11:23 AM – 01:53 PM | 9 |
| 2031 | Sat 20 Sep | Mon 29 Sep | 11:19 AM – 01:45 PM | 9 |

The "ten-day festival" is only sometimes ten days: the gap to Anant Chaturdashi is set by two tithis moving independently, so it runs nine to eleven days.

### 2027 — Saturday, 4 September

Visarjan Tuesday 14 September. The shortest madhyahna muhurat of the six years here, at 1 hour 3 minutes in Mumbai, because the Chaturthi tithi expires at 12:25 PM. Ten days of Ganeshotsav, and the sthapana falls on a weekend.

### 2028 — Wednesday, 23 August

Visarjan Saturday 2 September. This is the earliest Ganesh Chaturthi of the decade — twelve days earlier than 2027 and the only one of the six in August. Muhurat 11:25 AM to 01:57 PM in Mumbai, a full 2 hours 32 minutes.

### 2029 — Tuesday, 11 September

Visarjan Friday 21 September. An intercalary month between August 2028 and September 2029 pushes the date nineteen days later instead of eleven days earlier. Muhurat 11:21 AM to 01:49 PM in Mumbai.

### 2030 — Sunday, 1 September

Visarjan Tuesday 10 September. The only Sunday sthapana in this stretch, with a nine-day Ganeshotsav — the shortest of the six. Muhurat 11:23 AM to 01:53 PM in Mumbai.

### 2031 — Saturday, 20 September

Visarjan Monday 29 September. The latest date of the six, again after an intercalary month, and late enough that visarjan runs into the last days of September. Muhurat 11:19 AM to 01:45 PM in Mumbai.

## How to check any of these dates yourself

Start with the new moon. Ganesh Chaturthi is the fourth tithi of the waxing fortnight of Bhadrapada, so it lands three or four days after the amavasya that opens the month, and NASA publishes every new moon to 2100 to the minute.

For 2027 that instant is 31 August at 17:41 UT — 23:11 IST — and 4 September is four days later. Run the same test on 2028 (new moon 20 August, festival 23 August) and 2031 (new moon 16 September, festival 20 September) and it holds.

Then check the tithi window, because that is where almanacs disagree. A tithi is one-thirtieth of a synodic month — the time the Sun–Moon elongation takes to widen by 12° — so it averages about 23 hours 37 minutes and never lines up with a calendar day.

The lunation is not even a fixed length. [A 2019 study in the *Iraqi Journal of Physics*](https://doi.org/10.30723/ijp.v14i29.229) modelled every synodic month from 2000 to 2100 and found a mean of 29.53109 days, a shortest of 29.27436 days beginning 16 January 2053 and a longest of 29.81442 days beginning 27 November 2008 — a spread of about thirteen hours. A date this far out has to be computed from real lunar positions, not extrapolated by subtracting eleven days from last year.

## Planning a festival whose date will not sit still

Weekdays matter more than most people expect. Of the next five years, 2027 and 2031 are Saturdays and 2030 a Sunday, while 2028 falls on a Wednesday and 2029 on a Tuesday — which decides whether relatives travel.

The people who cannot travel are the reason to plan the message at the same time as the mandap. Across all 3,860 pages SubhSandesh has created since March 2026, spanning 15 page types, 49.6% of views arrive on a phone and 42.1% of creators password-protect the page before sharing it — platform-wide figures, not Ganesh ones.

Speed is not the constraint. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.8 hours, sampled on 1,065 "I love you" pages — an evening's work, so the week before 4 September 2027 is early enough.

If you want the far-away cousin to do something rather than read something, the [Ganesh Chaturthi page the recipient performs themselves](/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) has them offer the durva, kumkum, flowers and modak, circle the aarti thali while Karpur Gauram plays, and write their own prarthana back. For other occasions in the same year, [browse every SubhSandesh template](/templates).

## What a Ganesh Chaturthi page will not do for you

It cannot hand anyone a modak, and it cannot put them in front of your mandap. If the person you are thinking of will be in the same city on 4 September 2027, invite them and skip the link entirely.

It is also worth being blunt about how new this template is. Here is what people have actually built on SubhSandesh since March 2026 — all of it platform-wide, none of it Ganesh-specific:

| Page type | Pages created since 2026-03-12 | Share of 3,860 |
|---|---|---|
| "I love you" (/love-gf) | 1,065 | 27.6% |
| Digital bouquet (/bouquet-gf) | 954 | 24.7% |
| Apology dashboard (/apology-dashboard) | 904 | 23.4% |
| Birthday page for a partner (/birthday-gf) | 257 | 6.7% |
| Ganesh Chaturthi (/happy-ganesh-chaturthi) | 0 | 0% |

Every number is measured 2026-09-08. The Ganesh template shipped days ago and nobody has used it yet, so there is no Ganesh-specific open rate to quote — only the platform-wide figures above, drawn from romantic and apology pages.

## Watch the page get built

Ninety seconds, start to finish — the aarti going round, the five offerings, and the box at the end where they write a line back to you: [Ganesh Chaturthi Wishes Online — Full Walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mpWiv5T59QY). More page walkthroughs on Instagram: [@subhsandesh_official](https://www.instagram.com/subhsandesh_official).

auditReport.honestAssessment: This is a next-cycle asset and should be judged as one. Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 is on 14 September, five days from publication, and this domain has no Ganesh topical authority at all — nothing written now will rank for the 2026 query, and the entire case for the page is that it has twelve months to mature before the 2027 volume arrives. Against the five pages analysed, all of which are panchang aggregators or calendar-spam that simply assert the date, an answer engine has two reasons to prefer this one: it is the only page that publishes the Ganesh Chaturthi date, the Anant Chaturdashi visarjan date and the Mumbai madhyahna muhurat for every year to 2031 in one table, and the only one that cross-checks those dates against NASA's new-moon instants, so the 354/355/384/353/384-day gaps between governing new moons visibly explain the two nineteen-day jumps in 2029 and 2031. The 12:25 PM truncation of the 2027 muhurat in every Indian city is a genuine finding no competing page notices. Two honest weaknesses: every first-party number here is platform-wide across 15 page types and none of it is Ganesh data, because the /happy-ganesh-chaturthi template has created zero pages, so the moat is thinner on this post than on a romance-template post; and the Gislén and Eade paper is cited through a Wayback capture because the publisher's copy at narit.or.th is dead and sciengine.com blocks fetchers, which is a fragile link. The India-official source for this subject, the Positional Astronomy Centre that computes the Rashtriya Panchang, was unreachable and its absence is a real gap. Ranking is months away regardless and depends on links this page does not have.
